hero.body: Resomix processes authorised catalogue recordings with PYXIS-1, creates a sonic profile for each track and makes the catalogue searchable through reference-based similarity. Start with one recording. Receive ranked matches from the same partner-scoped index.
hero.status: Guided partner evaluation · Authorised audio · Partner-scoped index
hero.captionA: ONE REFERENCE → PYXIS-1 → PARTNER CATALOGUE → RANKED MATCHES
hero.figureAriaD: One reference recording passes through the open PYXIS-1 ring into the bounded partner-scoped sonic index; the closest recording cells come forward and resolve into ranked catalogue results 01 to 05.
hero.figureAriaM: Mobile hero: reference recording, PYXIS-1 with the partner index, then ranked results.
hero.title: Make your catalogue [[discoverable by sound.]]

product.h2: One processed catalogue. Two verified outputs.
product.body: Catalogue Intelligence is the catalogue-scale application of PYXIS-1. Once authorised recordings have been processed, each track can participate in discovery in two ways: as a reference that starts a search and as a candidate that can be returned when its sonic relationship is strong.
product.outABody: Submit an indexed track or an approved audio reference and receive the closest matches from the partner catalogue, ordered by PYXIS-1 similarity.
product.outBBody: Retrieve the analysis of a processed recording across rhythm, harmony, timbre, structure, spectral character and energy when a closer examination is required.
product.note: Similarity retrieves related recordings. Track Intelligence explains one recording. They are connected capabilities—not the same screen.
product.tiPreviewAria: Compact Track Intelligence preview: structure, energy, tempo, harmonic and timbre fields with fictional demonstration values.

flow.h2: Start with one track. Return relevant recordings from your own index.
flow.body1: A catalogue track can use its stored sonic profile immediately. An authorised uploaded reference is processed first. PYXIS-1 then compares that reference with the prepared partner index and returns the closest catalogue matches in ranked order.
flow.body2: The system does not ask the user to build the result list manually, and it does not reanalyse every candidate during each search.
flow.figureAriaD: Two input routes — an indexed catalogue track using its existing profile, or an authorised reference upload profiled before comparison — converge into one reference profile, are compared with the partner index, and return automatically ranked results.
flow.figureAriaM: Mobile flow: the two input routes converge into one reference profile, compared with the partner index, returning automatically ranked results.

trackIntel.h2: Open Track Intelligence when you need to understand the recording in greater detail.
trackIntel.body1: Similarity answers “what is sonically related?” Track Intelligence answers “what does PYXIS-1 detect in this recording?” For a processed track made available within the partner scope, the analysis can present structural, harmonic, rhythmic, timbral, spectral and energy characteristics.
trackIntel.body2: This is a separate analysis view. It is not repeated beside every similarity result, and the user does not need to inspect it before receiving ranked matches.
trackIntel.figureAriaD: A wide Track Intelligence inspection panel for one fictional recording: structural waveform with labelled sections, energy journey, tempo and harmonic fields, and a restrained timbre view.
trackIntel.figureAriaM: Mobile Track Intelligence preview with structure, energy, tempo, harmonic and timbre fields.

value.h2: Let sonic relevance give deeper catalogue another route into discovery.
value.body1: Metadata, release schedules and editorial priorities remain essential. PYXIS-1 adds a different retrieval signal: the relationship inside the audio itself. When an older, niche, new or unreleased recording is close to the reference, it can be returned because of that relationship—not because it already has behavioural history or recent attention.
value.body2: Resomix does not predict demand, guarantee exposure or decide what should be promoted. It makes more of the authorised catalogue eligible to be found when it is relevant to the sound being searched.
value.mod1Body: Relevant older recordings can appear beside newer releases when PYXIS-1 ranks the sonic relationship strongly.
value.mod2Body: New or unreleased audio can be profiled and matched without waiting for streams, sales or interaction history.
value.mod3Body: One known recording can lead users or internal teams into relevant catalogue inventory they might not have reached through metadata alone.
value.figureAriaD: A horizontal release timeline: a recent active reference, an older quieter catalogue recording and three neutral candidates. One orange sonic relationship connects the reference to the older recording, which then appears in the ranked result list.
value.figureAriaM: Mobile: the recent active reference and the older catalogue recording connected by one sonic relationship; the older recording appears in the ranked results.

partner.h2: Add sonic retrieval without replacing the systems you already run.
partner.body1: Resomix is designed as a complementary discovery and analysis layer. During a guided pilot, partners can test catalogue similarity and Track Intelligence on an agreed sample. In a scoped integration, authorised server-side requests can retrieve similarity or analysis responses for use inside the partner’s own product or internal workflow.
partner.body2: The partner retains its catalogue, brand, licensing model and customer relationship. Resomix supplies the processing, sonic profiles, ranking and response layer defined in the agreement.
partner.figureAriaD: Four-part architecture: the partner product or internal tool calls scoped API access, which reaches the partner sonic index and returns either ranked similarity results or a track analysis response.
partner.figureAriaM: Mobile integration: partner product, scoped API access, partner sonic index, then the two response branches.

boundary.h2: Your private catalogue does not become a shared partner pool.
boundary.body1: Authorised catalogue audio, derived profiles and the searchable index are restricted to the applicable partner scope. One partner’s private content is not exposed as another partner’s catalogue result. Access, retention and deletion follow the relevant written agreement.
boundary.body2: Partner catalogue processing begins only with authorised audio and metadata supplied for the agreed service.
boundary.figureAriaD: Two completely separate bounded partner indexes served by the same PYXIS-1 capability with separate keys, separate queries and separate result lists. No line crosses between the two private catalogues.
boundary.figureAriaM: Mobile: the two partner indexes stacked and fully separate, each with its own key, query and results.

pilot.h2: Test PYXIS-1 on the music that matters to your team.
pilot.body: The right proof is not a generic accuracy claim. It is a controlled evaluation against a representative sample of your own catalogue, using references your team knows and relevance criteria agreed before the test begins.

s1.title: Scope the sample
s1.copy: Agree the catalogue subset, intended use case, authorised inputs and evaluation criteria.

s2.title: Deliver audio and metadata
s2.copy: Supply authorised recording files and the agreed metadata through the managed partner workflow.

s3.title: Process and validate
s3.copy: PYXIS-1 creates the sonic profiles, the partner index is prepared and processing issues are reviewed.

s4.title: Run known-reference tests
s4.copy: Use references the partner team understands and review the ranked catalogue results through listening and product evaluation.

s5.title: Review the evidence
s5.copy: Examine relevance, processing coverage, query performance and integration fit before deciding whether to expand.

score.w1: Whether the first results are relevant to the partner’s evaluators.
score.w2: How much of the agreed sample is successfully profiled and indexed.
score.w3: Observed response behaviour under the agreed pilot conditions.
score.w4: Where the partner elects to measure it, whether relevant older or lower-exposure recordings appear in reviewed results.
score.w5: Whether the analytical outputs are useful and credible for the intended partner workflow.

pilot.scoreNote: Evaluation measures — agreed per pilot. No pre-populated percentages, timings or pass marks.

closing.h2: Process the catalogue. Test the matches. Decide with evidence.
closing.body: Bring authorised audio, metadata and a small set of reference cases. Resomix will define a guided evaluation of catalogue similarity, Track Intelligence and integration fit without requiring an immediate full-catalogue commitment.
closing.support: For labels · Distributors · Publishers · Stores · Music platforms
